parsed.explanation: No trans criminalisation, no facility or custody ban, and no documented police or violence targeting. Traveler-facing positives are documented and in force: statutory discrimination protection in goods/services covering gender reassignment since 2007, hate-crime and hate-speech coverage extended to trans identity (July 2026), a conversion-therapy offence, equal age of consent, and same-sex marriage adopted near-unanimously — signalling institutional acceptance despite a polarized 2015 consultation. The main negatives: no gender-recognition route (a resident gap, but here it means the visitor is read publicly under their birth marker — an outing modifier, not a state-imposed universal exposure), no enforcement data on the 2013/2026 hate-crime provisions, and unresolved edge questions (border treatment, detention placement, whether the parent equality act/single-sex code extends). No documented unremedied universal exposure. Thin but structurally positive record places it in Reduced Risk, just below the strongest tiers.
